analysis: Both changed files are test-only. (1) ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift lines 46-51: when a benchmark specification pins a solo prefill stripe, the fixture now also sets the prefill chunk and step-token budget env keys from the default CBv2SchedulerConfig. This only affects the qualification-test environment dictionary that is passed to makeBenchmarkSession. It does not touch production code, the SSD cache gate, TTL, lookup-key derivation, salt scoping, or KEK handling, so T-041 and SEC-035 are unchanged. The fixture still sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT and an ephemeral key, and the isolation checks for persistentTestNamespace are intact. (2) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift head lines 181-204: a new test asserts that the prefill-chunk and step-token-budget env keys are forwarded by LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment, that unrelated secrets are excluded, and that the keys are not in WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys. It only asserts the allowlist behavior and adds no production code. Remaining unverified contract: the production change this test pins (adding those keys to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, and the wide-chunk default for measured families) is not in the supplied batch. If it ships, a reviewer should confirm that the forwarded values are validated and bounded, because they affect prefill geometry and resource use (availability, T-010/T-029 class). They are operator-controlled local env, so this is not a concrete regression from the supplied evidence. No findings.
